seen.extent: One leaf, two pages: letter of Mexico, 30 October 1830, "Dear Sir", unsigned, about 30 lines. From the second paragraph on, numbers separated by full stops stand among plain English words (for example "Some sharp sparring has 527 recently very polite and conciliatory"), 55 numbers with values from 1 to 614 and 4 signs (open triangle, blotted triangle, X, flourish); endorsed "Mr Butler / To J. S. M. / my private Cypher".
seen.cipher: A numeric nomenclator written into a plain English letter: whole numbers for words and phrases, signs for further values, plain words kept for the rest. No decipherment is written over the numbers, in the margins or on the neighbouring frames, and no key is filed with the letter.

3856.unvetted: CUL Or.1080 6.12 (PGP 19773): four lines of fast cursive strokes on parchment seen at 1600 px; the script is not identified (shorthand, siyaq, numerals or an Indic or Ethiopic hand) so it is not shown to be a cipher; PGP says "perhaps a shorthand or numerical notation". Needs a palaeographer (Bohak, Elbaum) or comparison with Judaeo-Arabic shorthand and siyaq before it can be called open.

3857.unvetted: T-S Ar.39.472 (PGP 20963): table of about 45 cells with red numbers, abjad headings, 4-3-2-1 numeral columns and non-word letter strings, seen in a native crop; it looks like a letter-divination (geomantic or zairja) table, not shown to be a cipher; PGP says accounts or calendrical reckoning are possible. Needs an Arabic magic-table specialist; do not offer as a cipher yet.

3858.unvetted: CUL Or.1080 14.13 + 14.25 (PGP 31451, 31508): amulet; 14.13 has seven underlined lines of alif-like strokes mixed with eastern numerals, 14.25 has a diagram, ring-ended signs and strings; seen at 1400 px. The stroke-and-numeral lines read as abjad numbers or an amulet number series rather than as an encoded text; not shown to be a cipher. Needs the red instructions on 14.25 read and a wafq (magic square) check.

seen.where: CUDL IIIF T-S K12.60 verso at 1572 x 2000 px, 25 Nov 2026; PGP record 41966.
seen.extent: Verso of a parchment legal fragment: a grid of about 20 ring-ended magical signs (charakteres), each with one small Hebrew letter beside it, loose marks below.
